subject: Novatek security questionnaire: geofence / retention / erase clarifications
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@novatek.com>

Cc: marco.deluca@novatek.com

Subject: Novatek - clarifications on geography, retention, and delete for Hosted API

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Our security team reviewed the questionnaire and had two follow-ups focused on Hosted API behaviors we couldn't fully cover live:

1) Region binding: if we select EU-only for a production model, can requests (or backups) ever transit through or be persisted in non-EU regions? We need an operational guarantee and evidence for procurement.

2) Deletion/erase: if Novatek issues a tenant deletion request, what is the end‑to‑end timeline (including backups/snapshots) and what evidence do you provide? Can you confirm whether ephemeral caches (KV/prefix) are retained beyond the customer retention window?

I've attached the specific questions as a spreadsheet. If you can point to an internal runbook or provide a short timeline we can attach to our RFP response that would be great.

Appreciate it —
Elena
Security Program Manager
Novatek

Attachment: novatek-sq-questions.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: irene.choi@redwood.com <irene.choi@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Novatek - clarifications on geography, retention, and delete for Hosted API

Elena — thanks for the clear list. I pulled together concise answers below and attached a short operational timeline and a network/dataflow diagram for your procurement pack. If you need formal attestation (SOC2 addendum / evidence), we can follow up with our compliance team.

Region binding (EU-only):
- Production tenancy can be constrained to EU regions at the tenant level. Control plane metadata (customer id, billing) is accessible from our control plane; customer inference payloads and model state for EU tenants remain in EU physical hosts and persistent storage.
- Cross-region transit is only used for failover when EU capacity is exhausted and only if you opt into multi-region fallback in the routing policy. We document the fallback list in the tenancy config and require explicit customer opt-in for any non-EU failover.
- Backups and snapshots for EU-tenants are stored in EU storage buckets. Cross-region replication is disabled by default for EU-only tenancies.

Retention and erase (hosted API):
- Short-lived artifacts (inference KV cache, ephemeral batch shards): default TTL is 1 hour; these are not written to durable customer storage and are cleared on instance shutdown or when TTL expires.
- Runtime logs (request/response traces): retained for 30 days by default for debugging/observability, configurable down to 7 days for customers under contract. These logs are redacted for PII by our ingestion pipeline.
- Persistent customer artifacts (model pins, customer upload blobs, audit exports): retained per your contract and deleted within 30 days after a formal deletion request; index entries are removed immediately and object data is scheduled for purge.
- Snapshots/backups: snapshots are retained per the backup policy. For an ordered purge after a tenant deletion we execute a three-stage workflow: de-provision (immediate), purge live objects (within 30 days), scrub snapshots (up to 90 days depending on retention class). We provide a deletion attestation and a purge summary when complete.

Evidence and controls:
- We can provide: (a) copy of our tenant deletion runbook, (b) storage lifecycle policy excerpt showing EU-bucket configuration, (c) an audit log extract (redacted) showing a prior deletion event sample.
- Keys/Encryption: customer data at rest is encrypted with keys managed in our KMS; EU-only deployments support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations (bring-your-own).

Next steps / proposal:
- I'll attach the runbook and a diagram. If Novatek needs a hard SLA that prohibits non-EU fallback, we can prepare a binding routing policy addendum to the contract.

Action items:
1) Kimberly will attach the runbook snapshot and the flow diagram (for procurement).
2) Jonas will draft a short deletion attestation template we can sign after purge.
3) I'll schedule a 30-minute follow-up (if helpful) to walk procurement through the evidence pack.

Best,
Irene Choi
Director, Security Solutions
Redwood Inference

Thanks — couple quick clarifications from procurement/security:

• For the 90-day snapshot scrub window, can you confirm whether immutable backups (tape/archival classes) are used by default for EU tenants?
• When you say \"index entries removed immediately\", does that mean data is no longer addressable but may physically exist until the purge run? If so, can you provide the scheduled job cadence for the purge run?

We prefer a purge completion within 60 days if at all possible for contractual language. If there are operational constraints, please flag them.

—Marco
Director, Procurement (Novatek)

Marco / Elena — thanks for the follow-ups. Short answers below and I attached a one‑page timeline and example purge log for your legal/ops teams.

• Immutable backups: we do not write EU tenant snapshots to immutable tape by default. Our archival classes are region-bound object storage with retention labels; conversion to immutable tape is an optional process that is explicitly negotiated (not used for standard hosted customers).

• Index vs physical objects: correct — after deletion request we remove all namespace/index entries immediately so objects are not addressable. Physical objects are scheduled for asynchronous purge jobs. Purge cadence: nightly job scans marked namespaces; deletion workers process queued objects continuously; final scrub passes run weekly. Typical completion window for standard tenants is 30–60 days depending on size and retention class. We can commit to a 60-day contract window for Tenancy deletions for Novatek and include the routing policy addendum prohibiting non-EU fallback.

Attached: novatek-sq-responses.xlsx (response workbook), data-flow-diagram.png (ops diagram), purge-log-example.txt (redacted sample).

If you want a signed attestation at the end of the work, Jonas will follow up with the template.

Best regards,
Kimberly Park
